cands.bio: Democrat from Hayward representing California's 14th District in the U.S. House since September 2026. Served in the California State Senate (2022–2026) and on the Hayward City Council (2018–2022). Former IT manager and consultant. Holds a doctorate in social work from USC.

controversies.text: Federal records show United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super PAC, spent $1,642,140 to oppose them since 2021.
Missed 0 of 22 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.0%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements including the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521, Equality California, Courage California, Our Revolution and the San Francisco Chronicle editorial board.

Her Ballotpedia survey also lists the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Indivisible, National Nurses United, UFW, and statewide officials including Attorney General Rob Bonta and Lt. Gov. Eleni Kounalakis.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Wahab's actions or stated positions on data centers, homestead property tax relief, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, gun laws, abortion restrictions, or school vouchers and charters. Her campaign site's issues page was cut off partway through, so later sections (including any on public safety or education) were not read. The page that discusses her SB 79 votes is a secondary source, so we could not confirm the exact votes. We also could not find the year she was placed with her adoptive family in Fremont.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: As Senate Housing chair she expressed skepticism that more housing supply would lower prices, said California must move away from "development, development, development", and called YIMBY zoning proposals "giveaways to developers". She has said she supports more supply if developers subsidize affordable housing and parking minimums are kept.
Campaign site platform for Congress: build more housing at all income levels (starter homes, condos, apartments, senior housing), cut red tape and speed up construction.

cands.bio: Democrat and BART Board Director for District 5 (appointed May 2024, elected November 2024). Former Mayor of Dublin, the city's first Latina mayor. Chaired Valley Link. Director of Healthcare Services for Alameda County Supervisor David Haubert. Earlier worked as a small business manager in the dental and health sectors.

endorsements.text: U.S. Reps. Zoe Lofgren and Adam Gray, Dublin Mayor Sherry Hu, Hayward Mayor Mark Salinas, the Alameda County Deputy Sheriffs Association and the Alameda County Firefighters Association, as listed on her campaign site.
Congressional Hispanic Caucus BOLD PAC, listed by Ballotpedia for the special election.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Hernandez was born or raised, or when she came to California. We found no records of specific actions or votes she took as Dublin mayor or on the BART board. The pages we had showed no stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, gun policy, school choice or teacher pay, or campaign-funding pledges. Her campaign site's Issues page was cut off partway through the immigration section, so the Climate Change and Innovation & Emerging Technology sections could not be read. Ballotpedia says she did not complete its candidate survey. Several claims about her record as mayor, such as keeping Dublin financially strong without raising taxes, come only from her own campaign site and were not independently verified.

local.label: Roots 55: Her campaign site says she has made Dublin home for more than thirty years. workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site says ICE 'has become a symbol of an immigration system that's broken and out of control' and needs fundamental reform. It also says ICE is deporting immigrants who contribute to their communities.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she will fight to protect reproductive healthcare and restore reproductive freedom by supporting legislation like the Women's Health Protection Act.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she will fight to give police officers, firefighters and emergency responders the training, staffing and resources they need. It also says she wants to shut down organized retail theft rings.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says that as Dublin's mayor she built housing at every level of affordability and pushed for homes near BART. It also says that in Congress she will work to provide incentives to build new housing.
